_doc: The unspent ceiling per research domain — read minus ruled-on, as of the day it was written. Generated by tools/measure_research_spend.py --rebaseline. RAISING A NUMBER HERE IS A DECISION: it says the project chose to read further ahead of its adjudication, and the PR that raises it says why. Lowering one is free and is what spending a domain does.

raised.why: T-0571 (PR #714) read Fergus's 1843 Chicago directory — 2,695 entries — into dev while this branch was open. The read is legitimate and already merged; this branch inherits it and cannot spend it. The ceiling is raised to admit it, NOT to excuse it: T-0588 (rank 2) spends the directory on the businesses layer and T-0587 already spent 67 of it onto resident cards, so this domain has live spend tickets and the number should come back down.

T-0575 read Hurlbut's Chicago Antiquities pages 28-36 — the American Fur Company chapter — as 19 claims, and ruled on 8 of them in data/research/books/crosswalk.json: 4 merges (Gurdon S. Hubbard, Jean Baptiste Beaubien, Jamie Kinzie, Mr. John Crafts) and 6 refusals, each anchored to the claim it adjudicates. THE OTHER 11 NAME NOBODY, AND THAT IS WHAT THIS CHAPTER IS. It is prose and mostly judgement: Hurlbut's 'Chicago was the port and point of a very limited district of distribution', Hubbard's 'this place never had been preeminent as a trading-post', Hubbard buying the company's Illinois interest in 1828, Astor selling the company in 1834, a batteau, a wine bill and a list of trade goods. This instrument measures NAME adjudication, so those 11 cannot be spent by it however well they are used, and pretending otherwise by inventing name-pairs would be the corruption the instrument exists to prevent. What they CAN be spent on is the town, and four tickets were opened in the same PR to do it: T-0594 (Hubbard's arrival date against a resident record that grades the same year 'reconstructed' citing nothing), T-0595 (the Factory House origin of jb_beaubien_homestead), T-0596 (a ruling in docs/LIBERTIES.md on how much fur-trade apparatus the scene may show, which the chapter argues should be LESS), T-0597 (the Kinzie half-brotherhood). The number does not come back down when those land, because they are not crosswalk rulings; it comes down only if a later reading of this same chapter finds names in it, and it should not be raised again for prose without this same argument being made afresh.

T-0578 read volume 2 (C-H): 1,987 kept cards, plus the 40-card precision draw this ratchet also counts as read. It did NOT read ahead of its ruling — T-0590's gate does not allow that any more. The same PR extended tools/rule_newberry_leads.py from volume 1 to every volume read and ruled the 227 new leads volume 2 offers under T-0590's own ladder: 546 leads on 947 cards, 146 candidates testable in a held work, 400 refused, 0 merges, 0 discriminators found. So the SPEND rose with the read, from 866 to 1,498 under the counting T-0592 (PR #727) introduced. What stays unspent is what has always been unspent here — the cards standing under no lead at all, a surname nobody in this town carries. Two measurement faults this exposed are on T-0602 and neither is an excuse: the precision sample's 80 rows count as read though they are re-readings of records already counted, and an unanchored crosswalk ruling counts as nothing, so crosswalk.json's one pass and five written refusals count as zero.

T-0598 stated civic/voter_crosswalk.json's source at the top of the file, and 99 rulings that were UNJUDGEABLE became judgeable. Not one of them is on a card: the 99 voters T-0493 matched to residents rest on chicago_voter_lists_1833_1835_irad and no resident record cites it. This ceiling is the size of that finding, recorded so it can be paid down rather than rediscovered — it was previously invisible because the instrument could not ask the question. T-0514/T-0515 are the mint and regrade tickets that spend it; nothing here writes a card.

NOT this ticket's read, and recorded here because dev is red without it. PR #738 (T-0557) registered the land_sales domain in domains.json and read 375 Illinois public-domain tract sales into it, and did not record a ceiling — so --gate fails on every branch cut from dev with 'no ceiling recorded', which is the gate working exactly as designed on a domain that entered the registry without one. The figure is what #738 read and has not yet ruled on; its own crosswalk matched 17 purchasers, and the number should come down as that adjudication continues. T-0598 takes no credit for it and asks that the next land_sales ticket own it.

T-0501 read Hubbard's autobiography — 92 claims out of a 226-leaf book of PROSE, and prose is the case this measure was not built for. Its unit is a sentence, not a name: 66 of the 92 name no person at all, being the plan of Fort Dearborn, the Factor House, the sand spit, the old river mouth at The Pines, Mud Lake, the wild onion on the bank and the cornhills on the River Guarie. There is nobody in them to rule on and there never will be. EVERY NAME THE BOOK PRINTS IS RULED ON: 35 distinct persons, 7 merged, 15 refused (each anchored to the claim that names them), 2 exact matches, and 11 Illinois River and Mackinaw men the source never places at Chicago, counted and named in crosswalk.json's T-0501 pass. Spending the rest would mean inventing people to rule on. The ceiling moves once, for this reading, and the domain's next pass inherits it rather than a fresh excuse.

T-0499 read the first half of Fergus' Historical Series Nos. 26-29 on the owner's direct ask, and the reading is deliberately wider than its rulings. Of 41 claims, 36 carry no person this town could hold: they are landscape, buildings, streets, civic institutions and port statistics, and the crosswalk has nothing to rule on in them. Only five names in 429 leaves fall in the 1830-1836 window and ALL FIVE ARE RULED ON - two merges and three refusals - with every name outside the window listed by name in the pass so the next sweep does not re-examine it. The gap this raise opens is not unadjudicated names; it is town findings waiting for the structure and terrain tickets that will spend them.

T-0579 and T-0580 read volumes 3 (H-P) and 4 (P-Z), adding 2,439 records to a domain whose ruling tool had last run against volumes 1-2. The reading is the deliverable of two approved tickets and the ladder requires reading ahead of adjudication; what has not happened yet is the ruling pass over the new volumes, which tools/rule_newberry_leads.py performs and T-0590 established. T-0618's reader and the three page bands T-0619/T-0620/T-0621 will add volume 4's re-OCR on top of this, so this ceiling is a floor for that work, not a licence to stop ruling.

T-0506 read Fergus' 1839 directory entry by entry and crosswalked it against four pools, and the Norris 1844 and Fergus 1843 reads precede it. A directory entry is never an 1835 resident on its own - it is later evidence read backwards - so this domain is designed to stand far ahead of its spending, and the spending is the crosswalk adjudication plus T-0514 (mint residents from the consolidated evidence) and T-0515 (regrade the 727 letter-list-only residents). T-0611 will read the 1839 appendices on top of this.

The 1840 sheet reads (T-0565, T-0585 and the image-band tickets) added 31 named heads beyond the last baseline. 1840 is five years after the scene and can never be an 1835 residency on its own; the bridge work is apply_census_1840_bridges.py and the two resident tickets T-0514/T-0515, both open and queued.

T-0643 read 32 more lines of 33S7-9YYJ-8D and rules on none of them: the ticket forbids it, because the 1840 bridge to an 1835 resident is a separate adjudication (T-0505, T-0514, T-0515) and 1839/1840 alone is never a resident. Reading ahead of that bridge is the method working. This raise also absorbs the reading the other three census slices of this hour landed on dev — the ceiling was already blown at 5acb2977 before this branch merged, and it is one shared per-domain number. It is deliberately a ceiling to be TAKEN BACK: --tighten is free, and the moment the bridge tickets spend these names the ceiling should come down to what the domain has earned.

T-0529 read 33S7-9YYJ-V2, printed 237, and found it is the enumeration's RECAPITULATION sheet: thirty division totals, six footings and a grand total of 4,470 for the city. Its one claim names NOBODY and cannot be spent, now or ever — no line of it is a household, so there is no head to rule on, no serial to attach and nothing to cross into the town. The ceiling moves by one for a claim that is structurally unspendable, not for a name left unadjudicated.

T-0527 read the three remaining filled left sheets of images 26-50 (printed 227, 239 and 241) line by line: 83 more named heads. T-0495 forbids this ticket minting or regrading anybody - T-0505 crosswalks these readings and T-0514/T-0515 rule on the names - so the reading is deliberately ahead of its adjudication and the ceiling moves once, on purpose, rather than the gate being routed around.

T-0632 opened this hop for the directories domain and closed it in the same pass. tools/spend_directories.py rules on the 235 single-entry matches the four directory crosswalks already held, and writes each one onto the household record it names — the later trade, the later address and the source id, as graded values that describe 1839, 1843 or 1844 and touch no 1835 claim. So the ceiling is recorded at ZERO, which is what the domain now stands at: every ruling that reaches a person reaches that person's card. It is written down rather than left absent because the gate faults on an unrecorded ceiling, and because a zero somebody chose is a ratchet while an absence is a hole. Nothing here may drift back up: a later directory reading that rules on a person and does not reach their card raises this number and the gate says so.

T-0664 read the 1837 charter election and its list of voters for mayor out of Fergus 1839, printed pages 40-46: 765 claims, of which 706 are voters. It is a POLL, not a directory of names to be ruled on one by one — its whole yield is the crosswalk it feeds, and that is committed in the same PR: 190 letter-list persons, 82 entries off the 1833-1835 poll and tax lists and 53 residents of the town are now met by a second independent book, which is the second source the ratified ladder asks for. Ruling those onto cards is T-0514's and T-0515's to do and is forbidden to the reading; the consolidation series T-0634/T-0635 measures it.

T-0665 read Fergus 1839 printed pages 38-39 — the city register of 1839 and the printed tables of mayors and sheriffs — for 111 new claims. They are UNSPENDABLE by design, not unspent by neglect: Chicago was not a city until March 1837, so every office on printed page 38 postdates the scene date and nothing in the register may be written onto an 1835 record. The crosswalk in fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json rules on all 105 indexable names against the four pools and files 10 resident matches, 8 ambiguous, 25 surname-only refusals and 3 entries the rule cannot test; T-0514 and T-0515 are the passes allowed to carry any of it onto a card. The one row that reaches 1835 — Silas W. Sherman, sheriff of Cook County under the term the 1834 row opens — is filed as a derivation with its refusal and writes nothing to the town.

T-0514 seated 531 new residents and the land-sales resident crosswalk re-derived against the larger town. Its rule matches a purchaser only where the residents layer holds EXACTLY ONE person of the surname and the forename agrees, so a bigger town makes that rule fire less: nine matches became ambiguous (Carpenter, Dole, Fullerton, Haddock x2, Heacock, Sweet, Burdick, Wooley) and six became possible for the first time (Bronson, Hale, Hartzell, Ludby, Price, Wolcott), a net loss of three rulings with nothing new read. The ceiling moves by that difference rather than the domain being re-read. T-0670 carries the matcher's surname-uniqueness weakness and T-0609 is the ticket that spends this domain properly.

T-0675 walked T39N R14E sections 16, 21 and 29 to their end through the results page's own More cursor, which T-0557 had taken for a dead end. The reading grows from 375 sales to 566 — 191 of them the 1833 school-section auction the ceiling had hidden — and this ticket reads the register, it does not rule on it. Spending them is the standing work of T-0514 and T-0515, which is where a purchaser meets a person; nothing here mints or regrades anybody.

T-0500 read the second half of Fergus' Historical Series Nos. 26-29 — 58 claims and 45 town findings — completing the volume T-0499 began. The reading is deliberately wider than its rulings for the reason the first half already recorded: most of what these numbers carry is landscape, buildings, streets, civic institutions and port statistics, which the resident crosswalk has nothing to rule on. The names that DO fall in the 1830-1836 window are ruled on in the same pass; what this ceiling holds open is town findings waiting on the structure and terrain tickets that will spend them. Re-measured against the merged tree rather than carried over from this branch's earlier raise, because the baseline has moved several times since.

T-0589 read the civic account of Fergus's 1843 directory, page 1 lines 37-750: 388 claims, of which 264 are the town's own account of itself — the ward population count of 1 August 1843, the port's trade tables, the churches and their memberships, the offices and companies — and not names awaiting a crosswalk. 124 office-holder rows name 215 Chicagoans and are what the next crosswalk pass has to rule on. The ceiling moves by the reading; the spend it owes is T-0635's consolidation and the 1843 crosswalk, not this ticket.

T-0670 tightened the directory crosswalks to refuse a match where both readings print a full forename and the two disagree (Thomas L. Abbott was being merged onto Titus H. Abbott). 147 joins across Fergus 1843 and Norris 1844 are refused and 11 net rulings go with them: a resident whose only route to a printed claim was a bad initial-match no longer rules on it at all. The reading did not shrink; the town stopped claiming to have adjudicated eleven entries it had adjudicated wrongly. T-0696 is where the second discriminator that would win some of them back is decided.

T-0635 (consolidation pass 2) made these thirty-five visible; it did not create them. The second hop could not see land_sales at all until this pass taught it two things: that a ruling filed under `matches` declares itself a match by the name of its container, and that resident_crosswalk.json states what it rests on (T-0598's narrow form, added to tools/read_land_sales.py in the same PR). With both, the domain's purchaser matches — Hiram Pearsons, Walter Loomis Newberry, Daniel Elston, Thomas Hartzell and the rest, each naming a household_id and a resident_id — are judgeable for the first time, and NOT ONE is on the card it names. The count is 35 rather than the 14 this pass first measured because T-0675 and T-0676 (PRs #798, #816) read the ring townships and the paged sections while this pass was in flight, taking the register from 375 sales to 953 and its matches from 14 to 35. The ceiling is the size of that finding, recorded so it is paid down rather than rediscovered. This pass does not pay it: resident_crosswalk.json's own note assigns the spend to T-0514 and T-0515, T-0514 is closed and did not take it, and T-0515 is live in the queue as another run's row. T-0677 is filed to spend it, and a working tools/spend_land_sales.py is pushed on the branch steward/salvage-t0635-mine for whoever takes it. The number comes down when that lands and it may not drift up.

NOT THIS PASS'S DEBT, AND NOT A DRIFT BACK UP THROUGH NEGLECT. T-0632 pinned this hop at zero and said what would raise it: 'a later directory reading that rules on a person and does not reach their card raises this number and the gate says so'. That is exactly what happened. T-0666 (PR #791) read Fergus 1839's Fort Dearborn Addition lot sale of June 1839 and crosswalked 100 bidders against the town; 11 of them match a resident and 3 of those 11 name a card that cites nothing the ruling rests on. T-0635 is the pass that can SEE them — the second hop could not read a ruling grouped under a pool until this PR taught it to, so #791 merged green against an instrument that was not asking. The number is 3, it is T-0666's to pay, and T-0681 is filed to pay it by extending tools/spend_fergus_1839_later_lists.py to the third crosswalk of the same volume, which has the same shape, the same source id and the same carry rule. This pass does not take it: it would mean rewriting this PR's ledger and its counts after its verification had already been run, and the 101 rulings it does write are already gated in both directions. The ceiling comes back down to 0 when T-0681 lands.

T-0583 read all 2,255 lines of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago's roll of 1842-1892, the work fifty-four Newberry index cards cite and this project did not hold. Every line of it is LATER evidence — the roll opens seven years after the scene date — so none of it can be ruled on by the town the way an 1835 list is, and its crosswalk mints nobody. The unspent count it adds is the size of a source located and read, not a backlog of adjudication the town owes.

T-0502 read H. H. Porter's Short Autobiography (1915) end to end and the finding is that it carries no document of Chicago 1830-1836. Eight claims were filed; five of them are the evidence of the two identity refusals this pass wrote and are spent. The other three rule on nobody and cannot: bk_porter_006 and bk_porter_007 are town findings that describe 1853 - the Fort Dearborn blockhouse still standing, and the street grade five to twelve feet below 1904's - and bk_porter_008 states the volume's own distance from everything. A carries-no-document finding necessarily reads further ahead of its adjudication, because what it read names nobody this town holds. The alternative was to file the ruling and not the three readings, which would leave the next run to re-read seventy leaves to learn the same nothing. +3, deliberately.

T-0742 read printed 233 and 235 to the name - 55 more named lines off the sheets, and the last two of PR #670's seven calibration pages. Ruling on them is not this ticket's job and may not be faked to hold a ratchet: the 1840 bridge is T-0505's, over a deposit that is deliberately read ahead of it. The ceiling rises by exactly what was read.

T-0592 added three claims to town_findings_andreas_v1.json (c012-c014) that carry no town person to rule on: the trustees' $95.50 well of 10 Nov 1834, the water carts that served the town from the lake instead, and the Hydraulic Company's 1836 charter. They are town findings about water supply, quoted for docs/RESEARCH/wells.md, and the spend they demand is a ruling rather than a name — which the ticket made in full. Reclaim with --tighten once the civic domain next spends.

T-0679 restores the Fergus 1839 population table's 1840 line off the page image (4,479). It is a civic figure with town_finding: true and no name in it, so it adds one unspent unit that no ruling can ever spend; the ceiling takes the one rather than the row being dropped.

T-0724: one ruling was retired, not skipped. The 1843 and 1844 crosswalks each recorded a refusal reading 'the surname Horn is in Fergus 1843 and no entry under it carries the initial C of Cornelius C Van Horn' — a refusal that only existed because the splitter had truncated Van Horn to Horn. With the compound surname read whole there is no Van Horn in either directory to refuse, so the ruling is gone and the unspent count rises by one against a read count that did not move. No name went unread and no source was added.

T-0839 folded 42 duplicate town cards onto the people they name, and the spend measure dedupes a spend by its anchor: two crosswalk rows that pointed at two cards for one man now point at one, so the church domain's spent count fell by 30 without a single reading going unruled. The Second Presbyterian roll matched 92 residents and now matches 82 for exactly that reason — William Adams and William Hanford Adams were one man on two cards and are one row now. Nothing was un-read and nothing was un-ruled; the town simply stopped counting some people twice.

T-0839, the same cause as the church raise beside it: 42 duplicate town cards were folded onto the people they name and the spend measure dedupes by anchor, so directory rulings that reached two cards for one man now reach one. The four directories' spend re-derived to 294 people met and 587 rulings — up on trade and address reach, down on distinct anchors — and no reading was lost.

T-0678 registered the domain: 1,094 units read since T-0574/T-0577 (Fergus's 757 death notices, the three Calumet rolls' 327 names and 10 claims) enter the measure for the first time, and 657 of them are already ruled on. The ceiling is what the domain reads on the day it was registered, not a target.
T-0678 spent the domain in the same commit: all 109 rulings that reach a town person are on that person's card, so the ceiling this domain enters the baseline with is ZERO unwritten.
T-0678: both crosswalks state their source at the top of the file, so no ruling here reaches a person without saying what it rests on. Zero, and held there.

T-0724, re-applied after merging dev. The ruling this retires is the same one the ticket retired the first time: the 1843 and 1844 crosswalks each held a refusal reading 'the surname Horn is in Fergus 1843 and no entry under it carries the initial C of Cornelius C Van Horn', which existed only because the splitter truncated Van Horn to Horn. With the compound surname read whole there is no Van Horn in either directory to refuse. dev's own ceiling moved to 7228 under T-0839 while this branch was in flight, so the +1 is applied once more on top of it. Read count unmoved; no name went unread.

T-0837 spent the standing synthesis write, and the old-settlers roll re-derived against the moved residents layer: one name that had matched a card no longer does. No new page was read — 1,094 read is unchanged — so this is the town moving under a reading, not a reading running ahead of the town. Ruling on the 438 is T-0700's kind of work and not this ticket's.

T-0697. The reading did not move: all 953 records still carry a ruling, before and after (verified by diffing the record_ids of matches+refusals across the change — 953 covered on both sides). What moved is how the instrument ANCHORS a ruling. ANCHOR_KEYS ranks household_id above record_ids, so a matched purchaser dedups onto ONE household and a refused one dedups onto each of the records behind it. This ticket moved 100 purchaser spellings from refusal to match — the crosswalk stopped refusing on a count of namesakes and started putting the reading to every person of the surname — and their record anchors collapsed into 100 household anchors. The domain is spent MORE (34 cards to 124, the write hop reads 139 of 139 reaching a card) and measures 14 less. The ceiling is raised by exactly that artifact.

T-0714, 2026-09-06. The 1840 crosswalk was re-derived after 290 named heads of finished reading had never been put to the ladder, and the new adjudication reaches one town person the old one did not: Ira Couch, printed page 211 line 3 of image 33SQ-GYYJ-97P, ruled L7 candidate — the name agrees and is unique on both sides, with nothing independent of the name to hold the pair together. His card cites no 1840 source, so the ruling has reached the person and not the card. It is raised by exactly one rather than spent here because this crosswalk mints nobody and writes no household file by design; the write is T-0899's, on the ratified ladder, where a candidate stays a candidate.

T-0723 folded the duplicate card 'N. R. Norton' onto Nelson R. Norton, and the Second Presbyterian roll's crosswalk had carried a surname-only refusal against each of them. Retiring the duplicate retires one ruling, so the church domain's unspent count rose by exactly one (488 -> 489) without a single new line of church research being read. The ceiling follows the arithmetic of the fold, not a fresh read.

T-0581 read Moses and Kirkland's History of Chicago, Illinois, vol. 1 (1895) — the largest Chicago work the Newberry genealogical index points at that this project did not hold — as twenty claims, and its crosswalk pass rules zero merges ON PURPOSE. The volume is a compilation of 1895 that cites Andreas, Bross and Blanchard on the very pages read here, and it names men this project already carries from period sources: merging a compiler's spelling onto a witness's person would add nothing to the town and would make the identity layer's judgement off an 1895 secondary. Five refusals are written and only one of them can anchor to a claim (Spring / Giles Spring, a surname with a trade and no given name); the other four are index-card-versus-volume spelling pairs — blodget/Blodgett, caapbell/Campbell, gardiner/Gardner, mattoson/Matteson — which this instrument counts as id pairs and never as spend, correctly, because they adjudicate the sources' vocabulary and not the town. Of the twenty claims, six name nobody rulable at all (the State census trade counts, the open winter of 1834-5, Hogan's storehouse, Peck's store, the school-section purchase and the Pioneer Hook and Ladder roll of October 1835, which postdates the scene date by three months); the rest name people whose identification is a residents-layer judgement made under the ratified ladder in that layer's own PR, which is exactly what T-0581's third acceptance clause requires and forbids doing here. +19, deliberately, and the bridge work is filed rather than promised: T-0961 transcribes the volume's LIST OF ACTUAL SETTLERS AT CHICAGO PRIOR TO 1830 and T-0826 reads volume 2, against which every ABSENT verdict this pass recorded is an absence from volume 1 only.

T-0962 widened the second hop to read the container spelling `matched`, and church walked into the report for the first time carrying 82 rulings and not one card told. The debt is not new — second_presbyterian_crosswalk.json has adjudicated 82 roll members onto households since it was generated, and no resident record in the town cites second_presbyterian_chicago_1892 at all. The ceiling records that true figure rather than hiding it behind an instrument that could not see the container; it is a debt to pay down, and T-0992 is the ticket that pays it. It may not grow.

Mrs C. Taylor arrived in the town while this branch was open. dev minted hh_taylor_c (T-0960, PR #1050/#1051) and the Second Presbyterian crosswalk re-derived onto her: roll line second_presb_0870, "Taylor, Mrs. Charle's | Letter. | Januarys, 1843. | Dismissed.", printed page 203, matched on the same surname-plus-initial rule as the other 82. So the crosswalk's matched rows went 82 to 83 and church's write debt with them. The ceiling is NOT growing because church read further ahead — the reading is unchanged since T-0962 measured it this morning — but because the TOWN gained a card underneath it, which is the ladder working and not a hole opening. T-0992 pays the whole 83 down to 0 and this may not grow for any other reason.

T-0844 folded four town cards onto the people they name — hunt_c_s, kennicott_w_l, kinzie_john_s and temple_t — and seven rulings across these three domains had already been spent onto those cards by name. The reading did not move and the adjudication did not lapse: the rulings now name a person the redirect table resolves, and this measure's second hop reads a card id rather than following data/residents/index.json's merged table, which is the defect T-0962 owns. The ceiling is raised by exactly the count the fold moved (church +1, directories +3, old_settlers +3) rather than the rulings being re-spent onto the survivors, because re-spending them here would write the same paragraph onto a card twice — the fault T-0846 is open on.

T-0842 folded vanderbogart_h and vandenbogart_h onto vanderbogart_henry, so the town carries one card where it carried three. The old-settlers reading that had reached the folded letter-list card is not newly unread — it is on the survivor, at the same locator — but the ceiling counts CARDS the domain has reached, and the town now has two fewer of them. The +1 is the arithmetic of a merge, not research getting ahead of the spend.

T-0989 replaced the second hop's file-level source fallback with a test a card can actually fail. A generated crosswalk states its one source id at the top of the file, and until now a ruling that stated nothing of its own was counted WRITTEN whenever the card cited that id anywhere, for any reason at all — so a single citation put there by another pass satisfied every ruling in the file at once. 811 of the 1,359 person-reaching rulings in this repo were judged that way. A fallback ruling must now also NAME what it adjudicated: the read unit it cites, or the sheet a sheet-and-line ruling sits on. Nothing was spent or unspent by this commit; 255 rulings in directories that had been reported as reaching their card are now reported as not reaching it, and this ceiling records that true 255 rather than hiding it. The case, checked by hand: hh_garrett_a cites fergus_chicago_directory_1839 because a later resident-research pass wrote a generic directories block on the card, while Fergus 1839's ruling for Garrett — entry f1839_e0527, 'Garrett, Augustus, auctioneer, real estate, bds. Sauganash Hotel', printed page 15 — has never been written onto it. The number is paid down by spending those rulings onto the cards, not by raising it again.

T-0993 folded `blanchard_gantry` onto `blanchard_f_gantry` — one man the town held twice, the tax list of 1833 printing Francis Gurtrey Blanchard by his middle name alone. Nothing was un-read and no reading went unruled: this domain's crosswalk carried a REFUSAL made about the folded card ("The surname 'Blanchard' stands on the Second Presbyterian roll and no line under it carries the initial 'G' of 'Gantry Blanchard'"), and a refusal is counted as a ruling made. Fold the card and the refusal is no longer made — so `spent` falls by one and `unspent` rises by one, on a domain that read nothing new. The ceiling is raised by exactly one to admit that, and it is the arithmetic of a consolidation, not of reading further ahead. Every consolidation that folds a card will do this to every domain whose crosswalk refused it; the number comes back down as the domain is spent.
